verdict:
The two decisions stay, and no decision was added. D-PRE-31 and D-PRE-32 are real choices, but each had a wrong fact in its base, so I wrote both again. I also repaired the two fragments, closed.md, contract-changes.json, and contract-changes.md (written again from the JSON). The files of the author are in /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round7/decisions/contract-future/check/author-copy, and my notes are in /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round7/decisions/contract-future/check/notes.md.

Checks that ran: scripts/verify.mjs gives "OK: no failure" (67 quotes). build.mjs accepts both fragments and both decisions on a copy of r7 and on a copy of the working content (16 sections, 60 decisions, no error). Nobody opened the built page in a browser, and check.mjs did not run. No file of the worktree changed, nothing was written on GitHub, and no request went to production.

The most important finding is a source that the author did not have: the plan that the maintainer answered is in /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/timeline.jsonl, line 367. It changes three things. (1) Plan item 3 says "One pull request moves the history (D-CODE-04), and a second one edits the contract lines", so the move is first and CP-1 is second: the author had the opposite order. (2) The plan had the line "Send the two tested rewrites to Ariakit UI early", and its authorization list did not name it. (3) The plan listed the GitHub writes as "the branch, the issues, the pull requests".

Example of a repaired fact, D-PRE-32. The draft said "the service does not need a report". That is false for one of the two rewrites: the app has the 3 sibling rules today (apps/web/src/components/ariakit/styles/glider.ts:129 and :138, tabs.ariakit.react.tsx:561), and D-UI-02 says that the app does not edit a copied file. So the review page keeps that cost until Ariakit UI changes.

Example of a repaired fact, D-PRE-31. The draft said that the lab design reverses 5 UI rules. I verified 4 rules that it breaks and 1 that it extends (zoom keeps fit, 100%, and 200%). The rule for Approve and Reject is the earlier decision U02, not line 260 of the saved requirements.

decisions.question: The review design that you settled in the lab breaks some UI rules of the contract. How does the contract approve the design?
decisions.options: (1) with-each-page: no text now; each pull request that builds a page also changes the contract lines that the page breaks. It differs from answer 3 of 2026-10-07 for the UI rules. (2) rule-by-reference: one new row says that the pages follow the settled lab design at one tag; it lists the 5 verified differences and what does not change. The tag must stay, and it is public only after D-PRE-42. (3) rules-in-contract: write each changed UI rule into the contract; the contract stands alone, effort M, and nobody made the complete list. (4) layout-out: one line says that the contract binds what the review page does, not where a control is or how it looks.
decisions.recommended: rule-by-reference. It follows the two answers of 2026-10-07 (the lab is the reference on a branch, and the contract is updated first) with the least text. It is wrong if the maintainer wants a contract that stands alone on main (then rules-in-contract), or if he wants no layout in the contract (then layout-out: RULE-05, RULE-09, and RULE-02 show that the app already differs from three UI rules).
